Questions / Author

What do I owe the people who enter my stories?

Words make worlds. Worlds teach us what to notice.

Writing lets me imagine lives, choices and possibilities beyond my own. I want the worlds I make to invite attention: to people, to consequences, and to things a neat explanation can leave out.

Follow the questions ↓

A question to practise, not a finished answer.

Author

A story is a way of paying attention.

An invented world still makes choices about who matters, whose voice is heard, and what a reader is invited to hope for. I want to make those choices with care, while leaving room for surprise, ambiguity and a reader’s own response.

Where the question becomes concrete.

People

Who gets to be a person in this story?

A character should have room to want, refuse and surprise me. I want to notice when I have reduced someone to a lesson, a convenient obstacle or a reward for somebody else.

Explore attention to others →

Consequences

Does the world remember what its characters do?

Choices should leave traces. Worldwright explores storytelling in which a world can develop through connected situations and consequences, with its construction open to inspection.

Explore Worldwright →

Craft

Can the same idea find its right form?

A scene might want to become prose, a drawing, an animation or something a person can explore. Creator Studio is the developing workspace for bringing those forms into conversation.

Explore Creator Studio →

Honesty

What am I asking the reader to believe?

I want to distinguish invention from a claim about the real world, and conviction from certainty. Revision is part of taking both the story and the reader seriously.

Explore revision →

These commitments meet in one life. Each brings a different question into focus.
